name: Swift SQL query built by string interpolation (FMDB/SQLite.swift)
attack_scenario: A malicious value (e.g. name = ' OR '1'='1' --) interpolated with \(name) into the SQL string closes the literal and appends attacker SQL, turning a single-row lookup into an arbitrary read/write or auth bypass.
negative_test_hint: submit name = "' OR '1'='1' -- " and assert executeQuery returns a single row or errors, not the whole table

exemplar.noncompliant: let rs = try db.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '\(name)'", values: nil)
exemplar.compliant: let rs = try db.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?", values: [name])
exemplar.explanation: Swift string interpolation \(name) splices the value straight into the SQL text, so it is parsed as SQL. Use a ? placeholder and pass the value in the values array; FMDB/SQLite.swift bind it as data that can never be reinterpreted as SQL.
